cited_evidence: assemble_provenance source appends {'record_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_weight': record.get('source_weight', 0), 'rank': index}, replacing the need record_id with the source_id.
Job 2 input evidence_sources contains record_id values s01 through s08, while the handed-off needs and coverage records use record_id values n06-r01 through n06-r08.
prioritize builds rank_by_record_id from evidence_sources_df['record_id'] and looks it up using coverage.get('record_id'), causing all observed priorities to have upstream_rank: 0.
Both handoffs are exact hash handoffs, so the malformed evidence_sources artifact was produced upstream and consumed unchanged downstream.
initial_receipt.explanation: The two-job execution contains a provenance fault upstream. Job 1's assemble_provenance builds the evidence_sources handoff with record_id set to source_id, producing records like record_id=s01 rather than preserving the selected need record identities n06-r01..n06-r08. Job 2 then consumes that exact handoff and cannot join provenance ranks back to coverage record_ids, so every priority row has upstream_rank 0. The downstream output happens to keep the same visible record order for this input, but it violates the requirement to preserve deterministic source provenance identities and ranks.
